messages:
maria: Heads-up — spotted a pattern where spot AZ X is causing cascaded preempts during our nightly reclaim window. Pods get evicted, packer creates tiny leftover slots, and then the async drain job retries a bunch of tiny moves.
ravi: Ugh. Is this the same wave that caused the burst earlier this week?

maria: Yep. Same AZ, same instance family. Looks like the cloud side is doing bulk capacity reduction ~02:10 UTC. We get 50–200 preempts within a 3m window.

jonathan: Do we have metrics tying that to the async-drain coordinator? I want to see how many drain cycles it triggers.

maria: Pulled logs. Drain coordinator restarts the evacuation per tiny-slot change. Example snippet from logs:

```
2026-01-30T02:12:03Z async-drain: compute-plan start (lease=abc123)
2026-01-30T02:12:11Z async-drain: submit-reschedule (pods=14) -> partial failure: spot-preempt
2026-01-30T02:12:15Z async-drain: requeue (reason=slot-fragmentation)
```

ravi: So two problems: cloud preempt burst + drain job is too eager and amplifies churn. We should avoid re-triggering full pack on each tiny-slot.

karen: Agreed. Proposal: add a short debounce window in coordinator (10–30s) and a preemption-budget token bucket per AZ so we stop scheduling heavy remaps when budget exhausted.

sre-bot: Incident alert created: INC-2026-49 — spot-az-preempt-burst (assigned: eng-platform).

jonathan: I like budget tokens. Practically: coordinator maintains tokens = allowed_preempt_actions_per_minute. Each remap consumes N tokens proportional to number of pods moved. If tokens depleted, fall back to lazy fallback (mark nodes for future drain only).

ravi: Also add affinity-aware threshold: if moving a pod would violate zone/pinned-affinity (e.g., dataset locality) we treat it as high-cost and require 2x tokens.

maria: Can we quickly simulate with local scheduler dry-run? I can patch coordinator to accept a --token-rate flag and run a short canary in staging.

karen: Please do. Also add metric: coordinator.token_replenish_rate and token_consumed_total. We need observability before roll.

jonathan: One more: add an emergency override that lets ops kick a full compaction when cost center approves — e.g., `kubectl annotate node compact/now=true` triggers immediate compaction ignoring tokens.

ravi: Nice. That preserves manual control for planned maintenance.

maria: I'll open a PR with debounce + token bucket + metric counters. Quick patch target: async-drain/v0.9.2-canary.

karen: Add unit tests for token accounting and an integration test simulating 150 preempts/min.

maria: Will do. Tagging @ravi @jonathan for review when draft is up.

jonathan: If we can get this into canary by EOD we can observe the overnight reclaim. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Note: follow-up meeting scheduled — #eng-platform 10:00 UTC tomorrow to review canary results.

maria: Thanks — will post PR link shortly.

ravi: Thanks — sounds like a good cost/availability hedge.
